text:
Maya: Hey team — quick design review: compact dashboard chart I'm iterating on. Key things: legend density, axis label truncation, units toggles, smoothing behavior for noisy traces, and how we surface outliers. Posting mock + config. Thoughts?

Liam: Nice, looks way cleaner. main concern: legend is crowded when there are 8+ series. can we collapse/scroll? :thinking_face:

Maya: yeah — two options: inline wrap (multi-row) vs a collapsed dropdown that lists series with checkboxes. Inline wrap uses space but is discoverable. dropdown saves vertical space.

Sam: dropdown + a small always-visible summary ("3 selected") feels good on mobile. also keyboard accessible?

Devon: agreed. if we do dropdown, need keyboard nav and aria-expanded states. fallback: sticky mini-key on the right that shows colored dots and counts.

Maya: UXBot — accessibility checklist for both options?

UXBot: Accessibility quick notes:
- Dropdown approach: ensure focus trap not forced; allow arrow keys to move between items and space to toggle. each item needs an aria-checked and descriptive label (e.g., "Show CPU (avg over 1m)").
- Inline wrap: ensure contrast on labels >= 4.5:1, and hit target >= 44px for touch.
- Both: expose a single aria-label for the whole legend region and keyboard shortcut to toggle (e.g., `L`).

Maya: nice. another item: axis labels currently auto-format units (e.g., 1200 -> 1.2k). PR asked for an explicit unit selector (auto / raw / si). opinions?

Liam: auto is fine for most users but for billing charts we want raw numbers by default. maybe per-chart metadata to set default unit and an easy toggle in the header.

Sam: +1. add a tooltip hint: "Units: SI (click to change)" so power users discover it.

Devon: Also consider accessibility: screen readers should read the axis unit once, not every tick. `role=note` on the axis unit label works.

Maya: smoothing: currently we apply a 3-point moving average for 95th percentile traces. Some folks said smoothing hides spikes. Options: toggle smoothing per-series, or show raw on hover?

Liam: show raw on hover is good — microinteractions: when tooltip opens, overlay raw points and a small badge "raw". leave default smoothed for visual clarity.

Sam: and add a legend badge: small "~" icon indicating series is smoothed. clicking toggles smoothing.

Maya: outlier handling: we clip at 99.9 percentile and show a whisker + "n clipped" indicator. is that ok?

Devon: clipping without context can mislead. prefer showing whisker and an overflow marker (e.g., arrow) at the top with a tooltip listing top 5 outliers and option to toggle full-scale view.

Liam: overflow marker + option to expand scale on click. also make sure exporting CSV contains raw values, not clipped ones.

Maya: here's the quick chart config I'm prototyping: 

```json
{
  "legend": { "mode": "dropdown", "summary": true, "keyboardShortcuts": true },
  "units": { "default": "auto", "options": ["auto","raw","si"] },
  "smoothing": { "default": "smoothed", "perSeriesToggle": true },
  "outlierHandling": { "strategy": "whisker_overflow", "clipPercentile": 99.9 }
}
```

Sam: looks good. small copy tweak: change "summary" to "compactSummary" for clarity in config API.

Maya: noted. one more: tooltip copy — should we say "value" or something domain-specific (e.g., "tokens/s" or "requests/min")?

Liam: show unit on tooltip if known, otherwise default to "value". prefix with the series name to avoid ambiguity.

Devon: for hover, include a keyboard-accessible focus state (enter/space to pin tooltip). pinned tooltip must be closable with Esc.

Maya: decision proposals: 1) legend: dropdown with always-visible compact summary; 2) units: per-chart default + user toggle in header; 3) smoothing: default smoothed + raw-on-hover + per-series toggle; 4) outliers: whisker + overflow marker + expandable full-scale view. anyone veto?

Sam: no veto. approve :+1:

Liam: approve :thumbsup:

Devon: approve — will raise an accessibility checklist PR with the keyboard flow and aria attributes.

Maya: thanks all — I'll update figma and post a follow-up with screens. attaching fig link: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/metrics-dashboard-compact

UXBot: Reminder: update release notes for the change in default outlier handling so customers know display changed.

Maya: added to draft release notes. closing thread after I post the updated screens.
